claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar refractory high-entropy alloy.
The as-sintered WTaTiVZr material is single-phase or near-single-phase with a BCC structure.
WTaTiVZr can be produced by mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering in the stated initial condition.
WTaTiVZr has significant or severe lattice distortion relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure than pure tungsten during high-temperature service.
WTaTiVZr will have greater high-temperature fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The proposed improvement in plastic strain and toughness is governed by severe lattice distortion.
Thermally activated dislocation motion contributes to deformation in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion promotes the thermally activated dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion lowers the barriers for dislocation nucleation and motion.
WTaTiVZr exhibits enhanced cross-slip, dislocation climb, and dynamic recovery at high temperature.
Local stress heterogeneity in the distorted BCC lattice produces higher dislocation density and mobility.
The proposed dislocation processes make deformation more homogeneous, delay crack initiation, and delay brittle failure.
Pure tungsten has brittle-service limitations, including a high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature and irradiation-induced embrittlement.
Relative to pure tungsten, deformed WTaTiVZr will show more active dislocation processes and less cleavage.
The hypothesis is expected to apply at temperatures of at least 1000 degrees Celsius where thermally activated dislocation motion dominates.
The mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or when irradiation-induced defect clustering becomes dominant.
Pure tungsten and WTaTiVZr should be prepared by analogous powder-metallurgy routes and tested under identical temperature, atmosphere, and strain-rate conditions.
Secondary phases or grain-boundary effects may also contribute to the measured plasticity.
The role of long-term irradiation in the proposed deformation mechanism remains unresolved.
